review_items.rationale: Requirement and scope: the obligation fixes that a server must not treat a configuration as committed unless the log entry at that configuration index is a configuration entry encoding that configuration, scoped to one node that adopted an unpersisted configuration and later returned to the leader state with the vote of a fresh peer. Entry and caller duties: the whole path is exercised through public operations (BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, AddVoter) on two ordinary in-memory instances whose transports are connected in both directions, so no state is hand-built and no call edge is substituted. Legal history: node A bootstraps as the sole voter and commits its bootstrap configuration entry at index 1 and its own no-op at index 2 before the attempt; the configuration write is then failed once, which is the same leader-side path as the separately confirmed durability finding; node B is started unbootstrapped, so it holds neither a configuration nor a log and has no membership veto to withhold. Oracle: the property is an implication whose antecedent is the result event's own observation that the committed configuration contains two voters and whose assertion is that the log entry stored at that committed configuration index is a configuration entry; the assertion is a measurement of the LogStore entry kind at that index, not a precomputed expectation. Identity and correlation: the prerequisite phantom_config_adopted and the result committed_config_state share scenario=phantom-1 on the same test stream, and the admission check confirms the admitted operation produced this result. Observation path and completion: the result reads the live committed configuration and its index, then reads the log entry at that index through the LogStore with a nil read error, and reads the peer's atomic published configuration; the admitted operation produced a complete applicable result, the antecedent held (committed_voter_count 2) and the assertion was false (LogNoop, log_entry_is_configuration false) while the peer's configuration held a single voter. Contrary evidence: neither retained counterevidence applies here, because the node did not commit the configuration alone (the fresh peer's vote supplied the majority) and processConfigurationLogEntry is exactly the writer that never ran for this configuration. Wider consequence versus checked proposition: the checked proposition is that the committed configuration is backed by a configuration entry at its reported index; whether that state survives a restart and is re-derived from the log is excluded and remains open.

formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.

items.rationale: Requirement and scope: the obligation fixes that a server must not publish or commit a configuration change as its latest configuration unless the corresponding configuration log entry was durably stored, scoped to one configuration change attempted by a stable leader whose durable log write fails. Entry and caller duties: the check enters through the real Raft.AddVoter path, so the request is admitted only when configurationChangeChIfStable holds (latestIndex==committedIndex and commitIndex>=commitment.startIndex) and is then processed by Raft.appendConfigurationEntry, which builds the next configuration via nextConfiguration and hands the entry to Raft.dispatchLogs. Legal history: the harness waits for the single-voter cluster to be Leader with CommitIndex()>=2, so the bootstrap configuration entry (index 1) is committed and the leader has committed its own no-op (index 2) before the attempt; the operation is an actual leader-side membership change, not hand-built state. Oracle and legality of the fault: dispatchLogs assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs and pushes the future onto the inflight list, so the injected failure answers the future with an error and sets state Follower while appendConfigurationEntry continues to run setLatestConfiguration(configuration, future.Index()), commitment.setConfiguration and startStopReplication without inspecting the dispatch outcome; only the LogStore.StoreLogs call is faulted, and the fault is reported from the wrapper's own counter rather than inferred from the future's error, so the antecedent is an observed premise. Identity and correlation: the prerequisite config_append_attempt (attempt=config-append-1, pre_voter_count=1, pre_log_last_index=2) and the result config_state_after_failure (attempt=config-append-1, phase=after_failed_append) share the declared identity field on the same test stream, so the implication is evaluated on one admitted operation. Observation path and completion: the compared quantity is the live latest configuration's voter count read after the failed append, and the assertion compares it with the voter count recorded before the attempt; the admitted operation produced a complete applicable result, the antecedent store_failed=true was observed, and the implication evaluated false (latest_voter_count 2 against pre_voter_count 1) while the log still ended at index 2 and the committed configuration index stayed 1. Contrary evidence: none applies to this proposition; the two retained counterevidence sentences concern ordering protection (configurationChangeChIfStable) and self-healing by a later leader, and neither changes the observed post-failure state of the same node. Wider consequence versus checked proposition: the checked proposition is only that the node does not adopt a voter set whose entry is absent from its log; whether a node that later regains leadership would actually commit the phantom configuration is excluded by the unit scope and remains an independent open question.

formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.

open_details: The heartbeat fast path (Raft.processHeartbeat, installed by NewRaft and dispatched from NetworkTransport.handleConn) runs appendEntries off the main loop for pure heartbeats; the fields touched are atomic or lock-protected but the ordering against the main loop is unverified.
Raft.timeoutNow campaigns on the target without consulting the request term or sender.
The membership-change error path in appendConfigurationEntry continues to publish the new latest configuration and commitment after a StoreLogs failure that already set state Follower.

items.rationale: Requirement and scope: the obligation fixes that a server must not publish or commit a configuration change as its latest configuration unless the corresponding configuration log entry was durably stored, scoped to one configuration change attempted by a stable leader whose durable log write fails. Entry and caller duties: the check enters through the real Raft.AddVoter path, so the request is admitted only when configurationChangeChIfStable holds (latestIndex==committedIndex and commitIndex>=commitment.startIndex) and is then processed by Raft.appendConfigurationEntry, which builds the next configuration via nextConfiguration and hands the entry to Raft.dispatchLogs. Legal history: the harness waits for the single-voter cluster to be Leader with CommitIndex()>=2, so the bootstrap configuration entry (index 1) is committed and the leader has committed its own no-op (index 2) before the attempt; the operation is an actual leader-side membership change, not hand-built state. Oracle and legality of the fault: dispatchLogs assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs and pushes the future onto the inflight list, so the injected failure answers the future with an error and sets state Follower while appendConfigurationEntry continues to run setLatestConfiguration(configuration, future.Index()), commitment.setConfiguration and startStopReplication without inspecting the dispatch outcome; only the LogStore.StoreLogs call is faulted, and the fault is reported from the wrapper's own counter rather than inferred from the future's error, so the antecedent is an observed premise. Identity and correlation: the prerequisite config_append_attempt (attempt=config-append-1, pre_voter_count=1, pre_log_last_index=2) and the result config_state_after_failure (attempt=config-append-1, phase=after_failed_append) share the declared identity field on the same test stream, so the implication is evaluated on one admitted operation. Observation path and completion: the compared quantity is the live latest configuration's voter count read after the failed append, and the assertion compares it with the voter count recorded before the attempt; the admitted operation produced a complete applicable result, the antecedent store_failed=true was observed, and the implication evaluated false (latest_voter_count 2 against pre_voter_count 1) while the log still ended at index 2 and the committed configuration index stayed 1. Contrary evidence: none applies to this proposition; the two retained counterevidence sentences concern ordering protection (configurationChangeChIfStable) and self-healing by a later leader, and neither changes the observed post-failure state of the same node. Wider consequence versus checked proposition: the checked proposition is only that the node does not adopt a voter set whose entry is absent from its log; whether a node that later regains leadership would actually commit the phantom configuration is excluded by the unit scope and remains an independent open question.
items.report_title: 配置变更持久化失败后仍发布新配置
items.report_answer: 在单节点 leader 上注入一次 StoreLogs 失败后，AddVoter 返回注错错误、日志末索引仍为 2、已提交配置索引仍为 1，但该节点的最新配置已变为 2 个 voter、latestIndex=3，即采纳了日志中并不存在的成员集合；对应属性 latest_voter_count 等于尝试前的 1 被判为 violated。
limitations: One injected durable-write failure on a single-voter leader; a follower-side log append failure is a different scenario.
The check does not exercise the excluded whole-cluster consequence of regaining leadership and committing the phantom configuration.
The decisive read uses the instance's live configuration fields because GetConfiguration() carries no latest index; it is not an independent second observation of the persisted log.
The execution did not enable the Go race detector, so no statement is made about concurrent access here.

items.rationale: Requirement and scope: the obligation fixes that Raft.GetConfiguration must report, through the returned future's Index, the log index at which the node's latest configuration was written, so a caller can order or fence a later configuration change on it. Entry and caller duties: the harness calls the public Raft.GetConfiguration on the same node instance and then reads Index() on the returned future; it does not reach into the readout, and GetConfiguration() is documented as readable directly, so no main-loop-only precondition is being violated. Legal history: the harness waits for a genuine single-voter cluster to be Leader with CommitIndex()>=2, so the bootstrap configuration entry (written at index 1 by BootstrapCluster) is committed and the leader's own no-op (index 2) is committed before the read; the probe records that live latest configuration index, and the excluded configurationsCh path used by snapshot creation fills the same future type correctly, which is why the probe/readout comparison is specific to the synchronous constructor. Oracle: the property is a plain assertion, reported_index == probe.live_latest_config_index, evaluated only on the admitted operation, so what is measured is whether the caller-visible readout identifies the configuration the node is using. Identity and correlation: the prerequisite config_index_probe (probe=cfg-index-1) and the result config_index_readout (probe=cfg-index-1, phase=readout) share the declared identity field on the same test stream, and the admission check confirms the probe's operation produced this result. Observation path and completion: the prerequisite reads the configuration index the node is actually using (1), while the result reads the caller-visible future (0) and the Stats value ("0"); read_error=<nil> shows the zero was returned by a successful call rather than an error path, and the result also re-reads the live index after the call (1) so the discrepancy is not a race with a configuration change. Contrary evidence: the retained counterevidence that Configuration() is served from the same atomic copy the main loop published is consistent with the measurement and does not bear on the reported index; no current counterevidence contradicts the readout comparison. Wider consequence versus checked proposition: the checked proposition is only the index readout; whether an external caller's behaviour changes because of the zero is outside this snapshot and remains a separate question.
items.report_answer: 在已提交的单节点集群上，最新配置写在索引 1（已提交配置索引也为 1），但 Raft.GetConfiguration().Index() 返回 0，且 Raft.Stats 的 latest_configuration_index 同为 "0"，read_error 为 nil；属性 reported_index == 探针记录的最新配置索引 1 被判为 violated。

GetConfiguration serves the atomic copy, so the readout cannot be repaired by reading the returned Configuration(); the check records only the observed index.

items.rationale: Requirement and scope: the obligation fixes that a server must not treat a configuration as committed unless the log entry at that configuration index is a configuration entry encoding that configuration, scoped to one node that adopted an unpersisted configuration and later returned to the leader state with the vote of a fresh peer. Entry and caller duties: the whole path is exercised through public operations (BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, AddVoter) on two ordinary in-memory instances whose transports are connected in both directions, so no state is hand-built and no call edge is substituted. Legal history: node A bootstraps as the sole voter and commits its bootstrap configuration entry at index 1 and its own no-op at index 2 before the attempt; the configuration write is then failed once, which is the same leader-side path as the separately confirmed durability finding; node B is started unbootstrapped, so it holds neither a configuration nor a log and has no membership veto to withhold. Oracle: the property is an implication whose antecedent is the result event's own observation that the committed configuration contains two voters and whose assertion is that the log entry stored at that committed configuration index is a configuration entry; the assertion is a measurement of the LogStore entry kind at that index, not a precomputed expectation. Identity and correlation: the prerequisite phantom_config_adopted and the result committed_config_state share scenario=phantom-1 on the same test stream, and the admission check confirms the admitted operation produced this result. Observation path and completion: the result reads the live committed configuration and its index, then reads the log entry at that index through the LogStore with a nil read error, and reads the peer's atomic published configuration; the admitted operation produced a complete applicable result, the antecedent held (committed_voter_count 2) and the assertion was false (LogNoop, log_entry_is_configuration false) while the peer's configuration held a single voter. Contrary evidence: neither retained counterevidence applies here, because the node did not commit the configuration alone (the fresh peer's vote supplied the majority) and processConfigurationLogEntry is exactly the writer that never ran for this configuration. Wider consequence versus checked proposition: the checked proposition is that the committed configuration is backed by a configuration entry at its reported index; whether that state survives a restart and is re-derived from the log is excluded and remains open.
items.report_title: 未落盘的配置会被标记为已提交
items.report_answer: 同一场景走完后，节点 A 仍为 Leader，其已提交配置含 2 个 voter、配置索引为 3，但索引 3 的日志条目类型是 LogNoop，且加入节点的自身配置只有 1 个 voter；属性（已提交配置含 2 个 voter 时该索引必须是配置条目）被判为 violated。
limitations: The admission event was sampled about 200 ms after the failed write, by which time node A had already re-campaigned and committed, so its index fields describe the recovered state rather than the immediate post-failure state; the properties are carried by the injected-failure counter and append error plus the result event, not by that event's indexes.

The harness does not dump every log entry, so the premise that no entry anywhere encodes the two-voter configuration rests on the failed write, on the entry at the committed configuration index being a no-op, on the peer's own configuration containing a single voter, and on the corroborating earlier confirmed check of the same write path.
One fresh peer and one injected failure; recovery routes where a surviving majority repairs the log are outside this unit, as is restart behaviour.
